beforeReference.supportingExcerpt: Vanpouille-Box's 2017 experiments found that sufficiently high single radiation doses induced the DNA-degrading enzyme TREX1, reducing cytosolic DNA and interferon signalling. The threshold sufficient to clear cytosolic DNA varied from twelve to eighteen gray across the tested mouse and human carcinoma cell lines; a patient-derived lung-cancer xenograft was also examined. The work connected repeated lower-dose irradiation, type I interferon and dendritic-cell-dependent T-cell effects in defined models with checkpoint blockade. It does not supply a universal human dose ceiling, show that more physical injury always gives more useful immunity or select an individual radiation schedule.
beforeReference.explanation: TREX1 degrades DNA in tested models, with varying thresholds; no universal human ceiling, individual schedule or optimal immune dose is inferred. Abstract and seven selected body passages read. Cell/model thresholds, not a human dose ceiling or selected schedule. Complete raw abstract; only separately listed selected body passages were read. No whole-paper or whole-guideline reading.

beforeReference.supportingExcerpt: In a tumour, a tumour-associated macrophage is named for its location, and its state and tested functions are separate questions. A tumour can hold several programmes in different neighbourhoods or at different times. An expression cluster can suggest a repair, interferon or lipid-handling programme, which is a hypothesis; it does not establish that the cells suppress T cells, kill cancer cells or would respond to a macrophage-directed drug. One marker such as CD163 does not establish a universal suppressive state, a change in proportions between two biopsies does not show that the same cells changed state, and the plain statement that M1 is good and M2 is bad loses the tissue and experiment that give a response its meaning.
beforeReference.explanation: Earlier/later sampling and functional comparisons investigate a change without proving causation. Myeloid-state change is not necessarily malignant-clone change, and blood tumour DNA alone cannot identify an escape route. Named current field passage inspected for its assigned teaching; primary evidence keeps the earlier recorded depth unless separately listed as a fresh read.
